name: frequency-polygon
title: Frequency polygon
tagline: Frequency polygon of grouped data — derives midpoints, plots × at (midpoint, frequency) and joins; overlays up to three; occludable points; draw-it-on marking via place-derived.
description: A frequency polygon of grouped continuous data — points plotted at each class MIDPOINT against frequency, joined in order by straight line segments (an open polyline, never closed back to the axis), on arrowed, numbered axes with a light grid. You give the class intervals and their frequencies; the model derives every midpoint ((from + to) ÷ 2), plots a × at (midpoint, frequency), joins consecutive points, and scales both axes to fit (override with axes). Up to three polygons overlay on one grid for comparison, in distinct hues with a key. Occlude a class to leave its point UN-drawn (and the segments that would touch it) — the "complete the frequency polygon" question, with nothing on the canvas to leak where the point goes. Highlight rings a plotted point in amber (e.g. the modal class). showPolygons false draws just the labelled empty grid (the answer space); axes.showNumbers false suppresses the axis numbers too, for a "choose your own scale" grid. Hosted as a marked model tile with responseMode "place-derived", the blank answer space (showPolygons false, one series, numbered axes) becomes "draw the frequency polygon" answered ON the figure: a ghost handle per class waits on the x-axis at the class's lower boundary, the pupil drags one point per class into the grid (snapped to a tenth of a step on both axes, the live value shown under the pointer), placed points join in class order as they land, and each point is checked against the derived (midpoint, frequency) — both coordinates, no authored key.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever grouped data is shown as a frequency polygon: "draw a frequency polygon", "complete the frequency polygon", comparing two distributions on one grid, or reading a frequency / the modal class off a polygon. Give each polygon as a series with classes [{ from, to, frequency }] — write the INTERVALS, never the midpoints; the model computes (from + to) ÷ 2 and plots the point there. Common configurations: answer space — showPolygons false for the labelled empty grid pupils draw on (keep the classes in params so the axes scale to the data; add axes.showNumbers false when the pupil should also choose and label the scale); draw the polygon ON the model (auto-marked) — the same showPolygons false answer space on a MARKED model tile with responseMode "place-derived" and marking { mode: "auto", correctAnswer: { derived: true } } — one series with numbered axes only; a ghost handle per class sits on the x-axis at the class's lower boundary and the pupil drags one point per class into place (a tenth-of-a-step snap on both axes, live value under the pointer, points join in class order as they are placed), each point marked against the derived midpoint and frequency within half a small square each way (the frequencies belong in the question's table, the intervals in the stem — the figure gives nothing away); the choose-your-own-scale grid (axes.showNumbers false) CANNOT be marked this way — an unnumbered grid has no scale to snap or read, so keep that variant a posed answer space; complete the polygon — occlude true on some classes (their points and adjoining segments are simply absent; the completed figure belongs in the explanation or a later stage, never beside the question); worked example — series[].showValues true prints each frequency beside its point; comparison — two series with names, on by-default key, same grid (state comparisons in the block text: medians/spread in words). Staged builds read well: showPolygons false (the grid) → join false (points plotted) → the joined polygon → a second series added. Keep axes identical across blocks in one lesson so figures line up. The polygon is OPEN — it is never closed down to the x-axis at the ends, and points join in midpoint order. Switch primitive when the teaching changes: bars whose AREA is frequency (frequency density, unequal widths) → statistics/histogram; categorical gapped bars → statistics/bar-chart; a value over TIME with moving averages → statistics/time-series; cumulative frequency curve or box plot → statistics/box-cf; the working table (midpoint, f×x, estimated mean) → statistics/averages-table. Synonyms teachers use: frequency polygon, frequency diagram, midpoint, class interval, grouped frequency table, plot at the midpoint, join with straight lines, compare distributions, modal class.

series.description: The polygon(s), one entry per data set. One series is the standard figure; two (occasionally three) overlay for comparison in distinct hues — give each a name so the derived key can label them.

name.description: Display name for this data set, e.g. "Boys", "Year 7". Shown in the key (the key appears by default when there are two or more series). Omit for a single unnamed polygon.

classes.description: The grouped data — class intervals in order with their frequencies. The point is plotted at the DERIVED midpoint (from + to) ÷ 2 at height = frequency; consecutive points join with straight segments. Write the intervals, never the midpoints.

from.description: The lower class boundary, e.g. 15 for the class 15 < t ≤ 20.

to.description: The upper class boundary. The point plots at the midpoint (from + to) ÷ 2.

frequency.description: The frequency (count) in this class — the plotted height.

occlude.description: Leave this class's point UN-drawn — no ×, and no segment touching where it would go — the "complete the frequency polygon" hook. Nothing marks the position, so the figure cannot leak the answer; the class still counts towards the axis scale, so the completed figure (in a later stage or the explanation) lines up exactly. Default false.

highlight.description: Ring this plotted point in amber — the modal class, the answer, a point under discussion. Default false.

join.description: Join the plotted points with straight segments. Default true. Set false for the points-only frame of a staged build ("plot the midpoints first…").

showValues.description: Print each plotted frequency beside its point (worked/labelled version). Occluded classes print nothing. Default false.

showPolygons.description: Draw the polygons. Default true. false renders ONLY the numbered axes and grid, scaled to the data — the answer space for "draw a frequency polygon" (and the stage-0 frame of a staged build; the window still comes from the classes, so later stages align exactly). On a marked model tile with responseMode "place-derived" (one series, numbered axes), this same answer space becomes the response surface: the pupil drags one point per class into the grid and the polygon forms as points are placed.

axes.description: Axis windows, steps and titles. Everything here has a sensible derived default — set values to match a source figure or to keep several blocks on the same scale.

x.description: [min, max] for the x-axis. Default: the span of the classes (e.g. classes 15–35 give [15, 35] — the axis starts at the first boundary, not 0, exactly like exam grids).

xStep.description: Gap between x gridlines/ticks. Default: the smallest class width (doubled while the grid would exceed ~16 lines).

xLabelStep.description: Gap between printed x-axis numbers. Default: xStep. Use a multiple of xStep when every gridline numbered would crowd.

xLabel.description: The x-axis title — the variable with its unit, e.g. "Time (minutes)", "Height (cm)".

yMax.description: Top of the frequency axis. Default: the largest frequency rounded up to a step multiple.

yStep.description: Gap between frequency gridlines/numbers. Default: a sensible round value.

yLabelStep.description: Gap between printed frequency numbers. Default: yStep.

showNumbers.description: Print the axis numbers. Default true. false keeps the ticks and grid but hides every number — the "choose and label your own scale" answer grid (pair with showPolygons false). An unnumbered grid cannot host the place-derived response mode: with no scale to snap to or read, there is nothing honest to mark — keep that variant posed.

grid.description: Show the background grid. Default true (pupils read midpoints and frequencies off it).

showKey.description: Show a key naming each series. Default: on when there are two or more series, off for one. Set explicitly to override.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
